newsitem.title: CHILE: Drought-stricken Chile urges energy savings.
newsitem.headline: Drought-stricken Chile urges energy savings.

text.p: Chile, its rivers reduced to a trickle by severe drought, launched a national campaign Wednesday to get people to conserve electricity or face rationing.

Under the slogan "In times of drought, use energy wisely," the TV and radio campaign urges Chileans to shut off lights, cut their use of electrical appliances and avoid unnecessary power consumption at peak hours.
Central Chile, including the capital Santiago, relies on hydroelectric power for about 60 percent of its energy needs.

Drought in the area has drained reservoirs and dried up rivers that drive dam turbines. Water use restrictions have been in effect for weeks in a few parts of Santiago, where the Mapocho river has all but dried up.

The Association of Public Service Companies, a trade group of private power utilities, asked the government this week to draw up a rationing plan that would go into effect if conservation efforts failed.
The plan should include a timetable for blackouts, cuts in street lighting and a general reduction in power voltage, said the group.
Energy Minister Alejandro Jadresic said no rationing would be needed this year, but energy supplies would depend on whether winter rains fell as usual starting in June.
"We don't see any need to issue a power rationing decree at this time," Jadresic told a news conference.
The conservation campaign is aimed at saving about five percent of central Chile's regular power consumption, said energy ministry officials.
